findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in ApplicationController#set_locale, not in other paths that set the locale
findings.body:
`translate` still loads only `config.locale` (line 68). The new fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, and that is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159). Other code sets the locale without going through it:
- `app/jobs/base.rb:151` sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` in every Sidekiq job.
- `app/services/post_alerter.rb:138` calls `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`.
- `lib/post_destroyer.rb:102` calls `I18n.with_locale(SiteSetting.default_locale)`.

In a process that has not yet served a web request (a Sidekiq worker), a key missing from the active locale falls back to a locale that was never loaded. The result is `translation missing`. `translate` caches that result in the LRU (lines 71-76, key = key+locale+backend), so it persists until `reload!`. The feature therefore only works for web requests.

Fix: have `translate` (or `load_locale`) call `ensure_loaded!` for every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]`. Alternatively, call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` from the job runner and from the `with_locale` callers.

findings.title: LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain, so cached results go stale when default_locale changes
findings.body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. The value now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, because `FallbackLocaleList#[]` reads it (config/initializers/i18n.rb:17). The cache is cleared only in `reload!` (line 41), and nothing calls `I18n.reload!` when the site setting changes. After an admin changes the default locale, keys missing from a user's locale keep returning the old site-locale text until the process restarts. Consider including the site locale in the key, or clearing `@cache` when the setting changes.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! checks @loaded_locales outside the mutex
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` reads `@loaded_locales.include?` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`. `load_locale` re-checks inside the lock, so loading twice is avoided. The unlocked `||=` on line 63 is racy, though. If `reload!` sets `@loaded_locales = []` concurrently, two threads can end up with different arrays. This is minor, because `reload!` is mostly used in development. Simply delegating to `load_locale locale` would drop the duplicated check and the `||=`. The mutex-protected `load_locale` already returns early if the locale is loaded.

findings.title: Fallbacks are now enabled in all environments
findings.body:
The `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were removed from production, profile and the cloud66 template, and fallbacks are now installed unconditionally here. The development and test environments now get fallbacks too; before this change they did not. Specs that asserted a missing translation, or code that relied on `translation missing` for non-English locales in tests, could behave differently. Confirm the spec suite is intended to run with fallbacks on.

Also, `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, ...)` includes the module into whatever the backend class is at load time. Using `I18n::Backend::Simple` explicitly, as line 5 does, is more consistent.

findings.title: Mixed String and Symbol locales are not deduplicated by uniq
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq` assumes `locale` is a Symbol. `I18n.locale=` normalizes to a Symbol, but `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` is also called from the backend with caller-supplied locales. If one is passed as a String, the list can contain duplicates such as `"fr"` and `:fr`, which means extra lookups. Calling `locale.to_sym` would make it robust.

contracts.action: New fallback chain applied to every I18n lookup (Fallbacks module included in the backend, FallbackLocaleList installed as I18n.fallbacks)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously config.i18n.fallbacks = true in production.rb/profile.rb/cloud66 production.rb, which used Rails' default fallback list (default_locale only). The old path never loaded fallback locale files either.
contracts.before_after: Before: production only, fallback to I18n.default_locale. After: all environments, order [user locale, site default locale, :en]. The initializer sorts after 02-freedom_patches.rb and 05-site_settings.rb, so the patched Simple backend and SiteSetting exist. SiteSetting is read lazily in #[], at lookup time.
contracts.visible_effect: Missing strings in a user's locale render in the site locale or English instead of 'translation missing', but only if those locale files are loaded.
contracts.failure_mode: Fallback locales are loaded only via set_locale (web requests). In jobs and with_locale callers the fallback locale is not loaded, so the lookup still ends in 'translation missing', and that string is cached in the LRU.

contracts.action: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! called on each controller request after the locale is set
contracts.equivalent_path: I18n.translate in translate_accelerator.rb:68 lazily loads only config.locale.
contracts.before_after: Before: only the current locale was loaded on demand. After: the current locale, the site locale and :en are loaded per request. Each call after the first is a cheap include? check.
contracts.visible_effect: Translations from fallback locales become available to web-request rendering.
contracts.failure_mode: If a locale file load raises, the exception propagates from the before_filter and fails the request. load_locale does not add the locale to @loaded_locales on failure, so the next request retries. No silent failure.

summary: The change moves the locale fallbacks into one initializer and installs a custom chain of user locale, site locale, then English. The fallback locale files are loaded only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Sidekiq jobs and the `I18n.with_locale` callers (`post_alerter.rb`, `post_destroyer.rb`) still load only the current locale. In those paths a key missing from the current locale gives `translation missing`, and the LRU cache keeps that string. The cache key also ignores the site default locale. Smaller points: fallbacks are now on in development and test, and `ensure_loaded!` checks outside the mutex.
